speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, can you tell me if you have experienced any headaches, neck stiffness, or sensitivity to light? Also, have you had any recent travel or exposure to insects like ticks or mosquitoes?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have a stiff neck or sensitivity to light, and have you noticed any rash or recent insect bites? Additionally, have you experienced any confusion, hallucinations, or abnormal movements since starting haloperidol?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Fever and altered mentation. I also have Profuse sweating, Generalized rigidity, Confusion and disorientation, Ability to move all limbs, Normal deep tendon reflexes with bilateral downgoing plantar responses.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of haloperidol use and the presence of fever, rigidity, and altered mentation, I suspect Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome. REQUEST TEST: Creatine Kinase

speaker: Doctor
text: The significantly elevated creatine kinase confirms muscle breakdown, which strongly supports the diagnosis of Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome. DIAGNOSIS READY: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome
